subject: Performance lockdown: dedicated pool sizing & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Meyers <jordan@talltree.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita@talltree.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today's perf session

Thanks again for the demo and the deep dive today — super helpful. Quick post-call recap from our side so we have alignment before sizing: 

- Business goal: integrate real-time summarization into our customer support flow (zero manual batching, live stream to UI).
- Target SLOs (initial): p99 generation latency <= 180ms for 1-2 sentence replies, sustained throughput target ~60 req/s during peak (US-east region), expected concurrency up to 20 simultaneous streaming sessions.
- Typical request: average output 40-120 tokens, input context ~200 tokens; 80% of requests will stream partial output.
- Durability: must keep KV cache warm for pinned models between bursts.

We're open to a dedicated pool (Reserved) if you can show a clear sizing plan + pilot that demonstrates p99 latency under the above workload. Cost matters, but given SLA risk we're willing to accept a small premium for headroom at launch.

Attached: talltree_slo_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet with traffic profile + sample prompts), plus the call recording for your notes.

Next steps from our side: we can get NDA/pilot paperwork signed this week. Can your team propose two sizing options (cost-optimized vs latency-optimized) and a short pilot plan (3-5 days of distributed load testing) by EOD Monday?

Jordan
Director of Engineering, TallTree AI
(jordan@talltree.ai)

Jordan — thanks for the concise summary and the file. Good signal on streaming-heavy behaviour. I captured the top asks: p99 <= 180ms, sustained 60 req/s, concurrency 20, streaming-friendly output.

Action items (from Redwood):
- Karthik & Ben: produce two candidate pool configurations by Mon EOD (latency-prioritized and cost-prioritized). Include GPU SKU, reserved throughput estimate, expected concurrent sessions per GPU, and a short risk matrix.
- Ops: propose pilot test plan (3 days) including test harness, synthetic traffic profile, and acceptance criteria (p99, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization).
- Biz: I'll circulate the pilot SOW/DocuSign link once we have a sizing recommendation.

Preliminary notes (high level):
- Given 60 req/s peak and stream-heavy traffic, I expect we'll need a pool with multiple GPUs that favor streaming kernel performance and KV cache headroom. My quick gut: an initial latency-optimized option will likely use 4x H100-80GB equiv. (high memory, strong throughput for long contexts) and a cost-optimized option could try 6x L40s-48GB equiv. with tuned batching. I'll let Karthik validate.

Attaching initial sizing notes for internal review. Will follow up with the configs.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 19:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today's perf session

Couple of technical clarifications that will materially change sizing: 

- Average seq length (input+output): you mentioned avg output 40-120 tokens and input ~200 tokens — if average total is closer to 300 tokens we need to budget KV cache and attention costs accordingly. Please confirm distribution (p50/p95/p99) from the spreadsheet.
- Streaming: recommend chunked decode with 64-token chunks; that reduces p99 tail by smoothing kernel swaps but increases request count. We should account for the chunk overhead in throughput planning.
- Batching: continuous batching in our runtime will help, but enforce low latency by limiting batch windows (<=10ms) for the latency-prioritized option.

Preliminary config proposals (to be expanded for Monday):
- Latency-prioritized: 3 x H100-80GB (reserved pool), target reserved throughput ~70 req/s with expected sustained concurrency ~18-22 when using 64-token chunks and 10ms batch window. Higher headroom for p99.
- Cost-prioritized: 5 x L40s-48GB (reserved pool), target reserved throughput ~65 req/s with careful quantization (int8) and slightly higher batch windows. Might see p99 stretch to ~210ms under worst-case bursts.

I'll prepare a short benchmarking matrix (latency vs throughput vs concurrency) and include expected cost delta. Also adding a note about KV cache warming strategy (pin a minimal working set for the first 30s after cold start).

Karthik
Staff ML Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks like a good plan. A few quick replies: 

- Seq distribution: I've uploaded p50/p95/p99 columns into the spreadsheet (see talltree_slo_requirements.xlsx). p50 ~ 240 tokens total, p95 ~ 420, p99 ~ 780 (rare). Those extremes are important for your risk matrix.
- Prioritization: we're willing to sign for latency-optimized for launch if the pilot demonstrates stable p99 <= 180ms across p95 traffic. Cost-optimized can be a staged follow-up.
- Paperwork: I'll have legal send over a simple pilot addendum and NDA — expect DocuSign by Monday.

Please include the following acceptance criteria in your pilot plan:
- p99 latency measured over 4h rolling window must be <= 180ms for p95 traffic;
- sustained CPU/GPU utilisation under 70% at target throughput;
- no more than 0.5% 5xx error rate during the test window.

We want to target go-live for a limited cohort by mid-Feb if pilot looks good. Happy to jump on a 30min prep call on Monday if helpful.

Jordan
Director of Engineering, TallTree AI
